claims.text: The damaged component is made from Ti-6Al-4V.
The component has surface oxide contamination.
The component has service-wear-induced microstructural degradation.
Ion-beam cleaning or mechanical polishing can activate the Ti-6Al-4V surface before bonding.
Diffusion bonding at 700–850°C and 5–50 MPa under high vacuum or inert gas can repair the component.
Maintaining the specified atmosphere, temperature, and pressure will prevent liquid-phase formation during bonding.
Operating at 700–850°C will prevent hot cracking during the proposed repair.
Surface activation removes oxides and contaminants and exposes fresh metal surfaces.
Surface activation produces an ultraclean, atomically intimate interface.
An ultraclean, atomically intimate interface enhances grain-boundary diffusion.
An ultraclean, atomically intimate interface facilitates recrystallization in the joint area.
Moderate temperature and applied pressure promote atomic interdiffusion across the interface.
The bonding process produces a continuous, recrystallized joint.
Solid-state diffusion bonding avoids local chemical heterogeneities and hot cracks associated with fusion welding.
The diffusion-bonded repair will have greater interfacial strength than a conventional fusion-welded repair.
The diffusion-bonded repair will have superior fatigue resistance to a conventional fusion-welded repair under cyclic high-temperature and high-load conditions.
Traditional fusion-weld repairs of this system have a high risk of hot cracking.
Traditional fusion-weld repairs exhibit local chemical inhomogeneities and compromised fatigue strength under aggressive service conditions.
The proposed process is effective only within the stated temperature, pressure, and atmosphere boundaries.
Departures from the specified process window or scale-up to complex geometries may reduce bonding quality.
